t: For an additional amount for “Research, development, test, and evaluation, Air Force”, $17,000,000, to remain available until expended.

fable.w: This section is a bare appropriation of $17,000,000 for Air Force research, development, test, and evaluation. There is no tempting reading: it names no outside party, no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. It only makes funds available, so nothing crosses the federal boundary into a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing the expenditure of funds for Air Force research and development. It does not mention any consultation, coordination, public comment, advisory boards, or other forms of participation with entities outside the federal government. The text is purely financial and administrative.
qwen_block.s: For an additional amount for “Research, development, test, and evaluation, Air Force”, $17,000,000, to remain available until expended.

opus.w: This section only provides an additional $17,000,000 for Air Force research, development, test, and evaluation. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. One might be tempted to read a funding decision as a federal decision open to input, but nothing here brings any outside party into it.
opus.b: This section only appropriates money, so it does not involve participation. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing funds for the Air Force's research and development activities. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The definition of participation requires interaction with non-federal parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a decision is made, which is absent here.
qwen_chat.s: For an additional amount for “Research, development, test, and evaluation, Air Force”, $17,000,000, to remain available until expended.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "Research, development, test, and evaluation" implies some form of external collaboration or consultation with experts. However, the text is purely an appropriation clause authorizing funds for internal agency activities. It does not mandate any specific process of consulting with outside parties, nor does it establish a mechanism for public or external input into the decision-making process. The definition requires that the federal government consult or coordinate with people *outside* the government. This section only authorizes spending.
